cases.question: What voltage and maximum output current can the ESP32 built-in flash voltage regulator supply?

oracle_sources.title: ESP32 Technical Reference Manual
oracle_sources.text: The built-in flash voltage regulator can supply a voltage of 3.3 V or 1.8 V to other devices in the system, with a maximum output current of 40 mA.

cases.question: What deep-sleep power consumption does the ESP32 Series Datasheet state?

oracle_sources.title: ESP32 Series Datasheet
oracle_sources.text: Power consumption in Deep-sleep mode is 10 µA.

cases.question: For a single-supply ESP32 design, what supply voltage and output-current capability are recommended?

oracle_sources.title: ESP32 Series Datasheet
oracle_sources.text: When using a single-power supply, the recommended voltage of the power supply is 3.3 V, and its recommended output current is 500 mA or more.

cases.question: Which ESP32 GPIO pins are input-only, and what output or pull-resistor features do they lack?

required_facts.name: no output driver
accepted: do not feature an output driver

oracle_sources.title: ESP32 Series Datasheet
oracle_sources.text: GPIO pins 34-39 are input-only. These pins do not feature an output driver or internal pull-up/pull-down circuitry.

cases.question: How many UART controllers does ESP32 provide, and how much RAM do their transmit and receive FIFOs share?

oracle_sources.title: ESP32 Technical Reference Manual
oracle_sources.text: The three UART controllers are UART0, UART1, and UART2. Their main features include 1024 × 8-bit RAM shared by three UART transmit-FIFOs and receive-FIFOs.
